entries.name: Dire Wolf
entries.subtitle: Hunter of the Whispering Woods
entries.description: Large wolves that hunt in coordinated packs throughout the ancient forests. Their unusually intelligent behavior makes them far more dangerous than ordinary beasts.
notes: Usually attacks in groups.
Weak to fire damage.
Pack leaders are significantly stronger.
entries.lore: The wolves learned long ago that travelers fear the sound of one howl. They fear silence even more.

entries.name: Forest Wraith
entries.subtitle: Spirit Bound to Ancient Roots
entries.description: A restless spirit formed when ancient magic binds a dying soul to the forest. Wraiths move silently through trees and attack anyone who disturbs forgotten shrines.
notes: Highly resistant to physical attacks.
Arcane and fire attacks are effective.
Often appears near ruined shrines.
entries.lore: Not everything haunting the forest remembers that it was once human.

entries.name: Mountain Drake
entries.subtitle: Scaled Predator of Ironspine
entries.description: A smaller cousin of the ancient dragons, adapted to the freezing winds and rocky cliffs of Ironspine. Its scales are prized by armorers.
notes: Avoid its frontal breath attack.
The wings are vulnerable after landing.
Drake scales are valuable crafting materials.
entries.lore: The mountains belonged to the drakes before men ever carved roads through them.

entries.name: Ashen Keep
entries.subtitle: Seat of the Fallen Crown
entries.description: A fortress city built upon the ruins of an older kingdom. Ashen Keep serves as a refuge for warriors, merchants, craftsmen, and travelers.
notes: Contains the primary forge.
Merchants restock regularly.
The western gate leads toward the Whispering Woods.
entries.lore: The keep survived three kings, two invasions, and one dragon. Its people intend to survive whatever comes next.

entries.name: Whispering Woods
entries.subtitle: Forest of Forgotten Paths
entries.description: An ancient forest where trees grow around ruined shrines and abandoned roads. Travelers often report hearing voices when no one else is nearby.
notes: Contains several hidden shrines.
Moonwood can be harvested here.
Visibility becomes poor after dusk.
entries.lore: Some roads through the forest lead to places no map remembers.

entries.name: Duskreaver
entries.subtitle: Blade Forged in Dying Starlight
entries.description: A massive blade forged from dark metal veined with burning light. Scholars disagree whether the weapon was forged by mortals or recovered from something that fell from the sky.
notes: The blade remains warm even in freezing conditions.
Its inscriptions cannot be fully translated.
The weapon reacts to powerful enemies.
entries.lore: When the final star dies, Duskreaver is said to remember the light.

entries.name: Crown of Ashes
entries.subtitle: Broken Crown of a Forgotten King
entries.description: A shattered royal crown blackened by fire. Although damaged beyond repair, its ancient defensive enchantments remain active.
notes: Royal markings predate Ashen Keep.
Fragments emit weak protective magic.
Possibly connected to the Drowned Crown legend.
entries.lore: A broken crown still remembers the weight of a kingdom.

entries.name: Fall of the First King
entries.subtitle: Fragment from the Royal Chronicle
entries.description: The first kingdom of Aetherion collapsed after its ruler attempted to command powers buried beneath the capital. The surviving records disagree on what he awakened.
notes: The original capital may lie beneath modern Ashen Keep.
Several royal relics survived the kingdom's destruction.
References to a 'door beneath the throne' appear repeatedly.
entries.lore: The king sought immortality. What answered him offered something far worse.

entries.name: The First Dragon
entries.subtitle: Legend of the Burning Sky
entries.description: Ancient songs describe a creature of impossible size falling from the heavens in an age before the first kingdom. Its death reshaped the eastern mountains.
notes: Dragonfall Crater may be the impact site.
Modern drakes could descend from this creature.
Dragon scales contain traces of unknown magic.
entries.lore: For seven nights the sky burned, and on the eighth morning a mountain stood where no mountain had been before.
